title: Who wins the vote
scenario: One number shows up more than half the time. Which one?

intro.job: One number shows up more than half the time. Which one?

model_restatement: Find the number that appears most — more than half the time — and print it.

clarify.question: Is there always a majority?
clarify.answer: Yes — one number always appears more than half the time.

clarify.question: The number, or how many times?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Count how often each number appears. Then walk the counts, keeping whichever number has the most votes so far. Print the leader.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 4, what is winner?

why_line: max(counts) compares the dict's KEYS — 3, 2 and 1 — and 3 is the biggest key. It never looks at how many votes each one got.

explain.rule: max(counts) reads the candidates' names off the ballot box and picks the biggest NAME — 3 — without ever opening the box to count votes.
explain.bridge: So how do you tell max to judge each number by its count instead?

fix.rule: max(counts, key=counts.get): still hands back a key, but chooses it by looking up each key's count.

walk.gloss: Pick the number whose COUNT is biggest.

contrast.right_note: the number with the most votes

alternatives.note: Track the leader by hand — the same comparison, spelled out.

hints: After line 4, is winner the number with the most votes — or just the biggest number?
max over a dict compares the keys. You want it to compare the counts.

checkpoint.prompt: With the new votes, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — 4 has the most votes, even though 9 is the biggest number.

one_liner: max over a dict asks for the biggest KEY — to find the biggest VALUE you have to look at the counts.

choices.label: A list of votes — each number is one vote
A list of different numbers, no repeats
The biggest number in the list
The number that got the most votes, printed
How many votes the winner got

questions.prompt: With THIS list, which number wins? Work it out by hand.
3 is the biggest number in nums. Does it win?

choices.label: No — winning is about how many votes, and 3 got just one

hints: Count each number's votes first, then find the number with the most.
Tally into a dict with counts.get(x, 0) + 1. Then loop over counts and keep x whenever counts[x] beats counts[winner].

why.this_data: Your version is right — it walks the counts and keeps the leader by hand: 4 lines for the choice.
why.real_size: max can make that exact comparison for you in one line — same work, same speed, just shorter. Let's build it.

blocks.title: Count the votes
blocks.teaches: counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) + 1 adds one vote for x — starting from 0 the first time.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 2, after line 3: what is counts?

blocks.tile:
for x in nums:
    counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) + 1

blocks.title: max picks the biggest
blocks.teaches: max(things) hands back the biggest one.

blocks.title: Biggest by what?
blocks.teaches: max(things, key=f) compares f(thing) instead of the thing — here the length — and hands back the thing that wins.

blocks.title: Biggest number isn't most votes
blocks.teaches: max(counts) compares the KEYS — the numbers themselves. key=counts.get compares each number by its vote count.
